title: Relay Launch
premise: A neon-styled arcade launch game where the player times a relay launch by locking power and angle, then watches the projectile travel across a futuristic lane full of checkpoints and booster launchers.
interaction_model: Three-tap timing interaction: tap once to start, tap again to lock oscillating power, tap a third time to lock oscillating angle and launch. After launch, the game becomes an automated physics simulation until the object stops, then the player can restart from the result overlay.
objective: Send the relay object as far as possible and clear as many checkpoints as you can by choosing strong launch timing and benefiting from bounces and launcher boosts.
progression: Single-attempt score attack structure with immediate retries. Performance is measured by total distance traveled in meters and by checkpoint count, with dynamically extending milestone markers and occasional launcher checkpoints that create larger rebound opportunities.
theme: Futuristic neon relay/sprint arena with sci-fi sports presentation.
mood: Energetic, glossy, arcade-like, and slightly celebratory.
likely_audience: Casual mobile and browser players who enjoy short skill-based arcade challenges, timing games, and distance-chasing score attacks.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a timing-based projectile distance game built around power and angle locking.

Moderate confidence on fiction/theme details: the code uses a runner sprite, a coin-like projectile, and relay-themed text, so the exact narrative framing is stylized rather than mechanically important.
High confidence that checkpoints and launcher milestones are a defining secondary system beyond simple launch-and-land behavior.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished mobile-friendly browser arcade game called "Relay Launch" set in a neon futuristic sprint arena. The player should see a runner on a glowing launch pad at the left side of the screen and a small relay object or energy token ready to be launched down a luminous track. Use a full-screen presentation with a sci-fi HUD, dark blue space-like background, distant glowing skyline, bright lane markings, and sleek neon overlays. The core gameplay loop must be a three-tap timing sequence: first tap starts the relay attempt, second tap locks an oscillating power meter with a highlighted perfect zone, and third tap locks an oscillating launch angle shown as an aiming arc. Once the third tap happens, the object should launch automatically using projectile physics with gravity, bounce off the ground, roll with friction, and eventually come to rest. Measure distance in meters from the starting point and keep the camera following the projectile horizontally as it travels. Populate the course with checkpoint pillars every 100 meters and make every 200-meter checkpoint a special launcher pad that boosts and redirects the projectile on collision, so rebounds and lucky impacts can extend the run. Show the live distance during flight, play satisfying audio for start, calibration, launch, impacts, bonuses, and result, and use short impact/celebration visual feedback when the attempt begins and when it ends. After the object stops, display a centered results overlay with the final distance, how many checkpoints were cleared, and a single prominent button to launch again immediately. The game should feel fast to restart, easy to understand, skill-based, and tuned for repeat score-chasing attempts on desktop or touch devices.
